subject: Proposed role coverage and reporting shifts — engineering leadership draft
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed role coverage and reporting shifts — engineering leadership draft

Team —

Attached is a first-pass proposal for a modest restructure in Engineering focused on clarifying role coverage for platform services and tightening reporting lines for owners of inference runtime, orchestration, and observability. High-level goals: reduce handoffs on incidents, create clearer career ladders for ICs who lead infra initiatives, and rebalance manager spans in the Platform org.

What this draft changes (summary):
- Creates a new "Runtime Stability" group (3 EMs + 1 Staff) that reports to Jonas; consolidates KV cache, batching, and runtime ops staffing there.
- Moves two managers currently in "Serving Runtime" under Ava to report to Jonas to align on SLO ownership.
- Expands a Senior PM role (internal hire) to own rollout/rollback policy and canary config across Dedicated and Private.
- Adjusts manager spans: reduce average direct reports for Platform managers from 8 -> 5 where possible.

Risks and mitigations:
- Performance-review timing: proposed changes intentionally start after the ongoing review cycle completes; impacted individuals will be discussed in calibration before changes are finalized.
- Redlines to job scope: I expect a handful of minor scope clarifications; HR (Monica) will own communication and title changes.
- Operational continuity: temporary dual-reporting for 4 weeks during handover windows.

Attachments: org-chart-v2.png, reorg-impact-matrix.xlsx, proposed-comm-plan.docx

Ask: please review the attached and the inline notes on Confluence (link below). Looking for: objections, major risks I missed, and any blocking questions by end of day Wednesday (2026-04-01). If no material objections, I will brief Exec on Thursday and instruct Monica to prepare comms and 1:1 talking points.

Thanks —
Markus
Markus Klein
VP, Engineering — Platform
Redwood Inference

---
Replying to this thread will include HR and leadership by default.
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed role coverage and reporting shifts — engineering leadership draft

Thanks for the draft, Markus — solid framing. A few quick notes from my side: 

1) Performance reviews: as you noted we should wait until the current cycle is finalized. We should be explicit in the comms that no compensation or leveling decisions are made as part of the structural change; those will be handled separately in calibration. Otherwise we risk managers receiving pushback during review discussions.

2) People at risk of perceived demotion: please confirm that the two managers you propose moving have been given a heads-up or will be given a private 1:1 before broader comms. I strongly recommend we run a calibration readout with all affected managers + HR before Thursday's Exec briefing.

3) Career laddering: the Staff/Principal expectations in the new Runtime Stability group need explicit IC growth paths. I can draft a short addendum to the proposed-comm-plan with language for IC growth and mentoring.

4) Communication cadence: for team-level comms, suggest (a) private 1:1s with affected managers, (b) all-hands for Platform followed by small team meetings, (c) FAQ doc. Monica, can you own the FAQ and the 1:1 script?

Minor: please add an explicit timeline slice for the 4-week dual-reporting period and who will be the escalation contact during that window.

Happy to sync 30 minutes today if useful.

—Lauren
Director, Product Management
Redwood Inference

Thanks for looping HR in. Quick HR/legal read and next steps: 

1) Heads-up and 1:1s: agree with Lauren — all affected managers should get a private 1:1 before anything wider. We'll use the 1:1 script in proposed-comm-plan.docx as the base.

2) Review of job descriptions and titles: please route the updated JD redlines to me by Wednesday EOD. I will coordinate title changes vs. promotions with Compensation.

3) Outplacement / support: at this stage we are not proposing layoffs — the plan is largely re-reporting and scope changes. If we move to role eliminations, we need Exec sign-off and budget for transitional support.

4) Timeline sanity check: the timings in Confluence look aggressive. Recommend:
- Thu 2026-04-02: Exec brief (Markus)
- Fri 2026-04-03: Manager 1:1s begin (Monica + direct manager)
- Mon 2026-04-06: Team-level comms and FAQ posted
- Week of 2026-04-13: Handover window / 4-week dual-reporting begins
5) Legal review: I've pinged outside counsel (andrews_legal@outsidelegal.com) for a quick look at title language and any local compliance flags for EU employees.

I've attached a redlined comms doc and a very small impact matrix (reorg-impact-matrix.xlsx) with roles flagged as A (core) / B (adjacent) / C (support).

I'll be on the Exec call if you want me there.

—Monica
Head of People Ops
Redwood Inference

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the redlines; appreciate the calibration. Quick update and actions: 

- Exec brief is scheduled Thursday, 2026-04-02 at 10:00am PT. I'll present the rationale, timeline, and the impact matrix. Monica, please prepare the 1:1 schedule and the FAQ doc so we can move immediately on Friday if Exec is aligned.
- I incorporated Lauren's suggested language about reviews/comp calibration into the proposed-comm-plan.docx (see Drive link).
- I've marked the two managers for reporting change as "AFFECTED" in the impact matrix so HR has clear routing.
- Tara Ives will join the Exec call to offer an outsider's view on comms framing.

If there are any objections to the timeline as-is, say so before the Exec brief; otherwise I'll assume tacit approval and proceed to instruct Monica to begin 1:1 scheduling post-brief.

Best,
Markus
